events.title: Netscape browser discontinued
events.summary: AOL ended development of the Netscape browser on March 1, 2008 — closing the chapter on the company that once dominated the web.
events.about: Netscape's demise marked the end of the browser that launched the commercial web and the browser wars. Mozilla Firefox carried its codebase forward, but the Netscape brand — once synonymous with the internet — faded as IE and later Chrome took over.

narrative.whyChosen: Netscape's shutdown bookended the first era of the browser wars.
narrative.whyImportant: It cemented Firefox/Mozilla as the heir to Netscape's open-web mission.
narrative.problemSolved: AOL could not sustain a competing browser; users needed a clear migration path to supported software.

events.title: Steve Ballmer chants "Web developers! Web developers! Web developers!"
events.summary: At MIX08 in Las Vegas, Ballmer reprised his famous developers chant after an audience member asked for love for the web dev community.
events.about: Ballmer was interviewing with Guy Kawasaki when a developer in the crowd requested the ritual. The moment tied Microsoft's Silverlight and web platform push to the same sweaty enthusiasm as the 2000 original.

narrative.whyChosen: The sequel meme — developers chant updated for the web era.
narrative.whyImportant: It signaled Microsoft's courtship of web developers during the Flash/Silverlight wars.
narrative.problemSolved: MIX needed a viral moment to rally the web community around Microsoft's stack.

events.quoteText: Web developers! Web developers! Web developers!
